notes: Changed from one-thread-per-row (stride-D access, 12.5% coalescing) to one-block-per-row with warp reductions. Coalescing 12.5%→100%, occupancy 16.7%→95.8%, latency ↓87%.

hypothesis: Shared memory tiling with tile-size=16 to reduce global memory latency
notes: 23.9% speedup (0.9289→0.7068ms). Global Load Efficiency 56→100%, L1 Bank Conflicts 32.8M→4.43M. New bottleneck: Barrier stall 5.87 dominates from syncthreads overhead. FMA Utilization dropped 19→10%.
Fused normalize pass into shared memory: exp values cached in smem, eliminating one global read+write pass. Memory traffic reduced ~40%. Latency ↓34%.

hypothesis: Larger tiles reduce barrier sync count from 128→64
notes: 3.9% regression (0.7068→0.7342ms). Occupancy collapsed 95%→67% (38K regs/block, only 1 block/SM). Barrier stall dropped 5.87→2.59 but occupancy loss dominated. Lesson: 1024-thread blocks hurt occupancy too much.
Float4 vectorization: slight regression (~1.7%). Memory already saturated at 93%, float4 increased shared memory bank contention (Short Scoreboard 5.6%→17.6%). No benefit for bandwidth-bound kernels.

hypothesis: Distribute QK score computation across all threads with strided assignment and warp/block reductions instead of serializing on thread 0
notes: 4.1x speedup. WarpExecEff 1.73→32%, StallBarrier 14.41→1.36%. Now latency-bound with LongScoreboard=30.37%, L1BankConflicts=227M from strided scores[] access.

optimization: Unroll inner K loop with #pragma unroll
hypothesis: Unroll inner K loop to reduce instruction overhead and improve ILP
notes: No change (0.7068→0.7113ms, within noise). IPC unchanged (0.3046→0.3023). Unrolling 16-iteration shared memory loop provides no benefit — compiler likely already schedules well for such small loops.
__expf() fast-math: negligible change (0.2%). Confirms kernel is fully memory-bandwidth bound at 93.9%. Compute optimizations have no effect.

optimization: Fuse 2 K-tile loads per barrier cycle
hypothesis: Loading and computing 2 tiles per barrier halves barrier calls
notes: 2.2% improvement (0.7068→0.6911ms). Barrier stall unchanged (5.87→5.85) but Long Scoreboard dropped 5.34→2.99 (44%). More compute per barrier helped hide load latency. Shared memory 2KB→4KB.
__launch_bounds__(256,6): negligible effect (0.03%). Kernel at bandwidth roofline (93.9%), further optimization limited by DRAM bandwidth.

optimization: Pad As shared memory (+1 column) for bank conflict elimination
hypothesis: Padding stride from 16→17 eliminates bank conflicts in As[ty][k] access
notes: 43% regression (0.6911→0.9896ms). Multiply-by-17 address computation worse than 2-way bank conflicts (which are partially mitigated by broadcast). L1 Bank Conflicts actually increased 4.20M→6.30M. IPC dropped 0.2728→0.2224 due to extra instructions. Lesson: padding helps only when address computation overhead < bank conflict penalty.

hypothesis: Change thread-to-key mapping from strided to contiguous chunks to eliminate shared memory bank conflicts
notes: 2.8% regression. Bank conflicts unchanged (227M→217M). Root cause: L1 bank conflict metric tracks L1 data cache, not shared memory. Contiguous vs strided mapping doesn't change global memory access pattern.

hypothesis: Use float4 vectorized loads in QK dot-product loop to improve global load efficiency
notes: 1.71x speedup. GlobalLoadEff 22→66%, L1BankConflicts 227M→37M (-84%). float4 replaces 4 scalar loads with one 16-byte load. L1HitRate dropped 75→20% but L2 at 99.9%. LongScoreboard still 35%.

hypothesis: Add #pragma unroll on output weighted-sum loop and reduction loops to improve ILP and hide V load latency
notes: 1.26x speedup. IPC 0.10→0.14 (+43%), L1HitRate 20→44%, BarrierStall 2.09→0.24%. FFMA throughput 260→318. LongScoreboard up to 44.67% (relative increase from faster compute).

hypothesis: Add const __restrict__ to Q,K,V pointers to enable LDG read-only cache path
notes: Neutral (0.2% within noise). Compiler already routes const* through read-only cache on sm_86. Metrics essentially unchanged from v4. Kernel now firmly memory-latency-bound at LongScoreboard=44.5%.

hypothesis: Increase num_warps 4→8 and process 2 rows per block
notes: Regression: Memory throughput dropped 85.6%→77.7%, L1 bank conflicts ↑48% (2839→4192), register pressure ↑ (23→28/thread). More warps increased contention.

hypothesis: Revert num_warps to default (4) keeping 2 rows per block
notes: Further regression: Occupancy dropped 98%→53% (Waves/SM 1.02→0.51). Halving blocks (1024→512) reduced parallelism. Multi-row approach inherently reduces grid size, hurting occupancy.

hypothesis: Replace manual softmax with tl.softmax builtin
notes: Neutral: tl.softmax produces essentially identical PTX as manual max→exp→sum→div. Same metrics across the board.

hypothesis: Increase num_warps to 8 keeping single row per block
notes: Major regression +62%: Latency 0.0406→0.0646ms. Despite occupancy ↑93% and Long Scoreboard ↓30%, L1 bank conflicts ↑57% (2981→4452) and shared memory BW doubled. More warps increased cross-warp reduction overhead.

hypothesis: Reduce num_warps to 2 to reduce shared memory bank conflicts
notes: Regression +9.5%. Despite Long Scoreboard ↓30% and slightly fewer bank conflicts (2839→2753), register pressure ↑43% (23→33/thread) because each thread handles 16 elements. Theoretical occupancy dropped to 66.7%, IPC ↓20%.

hypothesis: Replace manual pointer arithmetic with tl.make_block_ptr with order=(1,0) for coalesced global loads
notes: No measurable effect. Triton compiler already generates similar code for pointer arithmetic. Global Load Efficiency remained 0%%. All metrics essentially unchanged.

optimization: num_warps=8 to increase occupancy from 25%% to 50%%
hypothesis: Double num_warps from 4 to 8 to increase occupancy and hide shared memory latency
notes: Occupancy doubled but Short Scoreboard stall tripled (0.70->2.64) from shared memory contention. More warps hitting SMEM created more bank pressure. Classic occupancy above all else anti-pattern.

optimization: Reduce BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N from 64 to 32 for more grid parallelism
hypothesis: Smaller tiles increase grid from 256 to 1024 blocks for better SM utilization
notes: SM utilization rose to 80.88%% but FMA pipe dropped from 59%% to 38%%. More blocks meant more barriers and scheduling overhead per unit of actual compute. Smaller tiles had lower arithmetic efficiency per tile.

optimization: Increase BLOCK_K from 32 to 64 to halve K-loop iterations
hypothesis: Larger BLOCK_K halves barrier count and enables more efficient per-iteration dot products
notes: Occupancy collapsed to 8.3%% (64KB SMEM allows only 1 block/SM). But L1 Bank Conflicts went to zero and Barrier stall dropped 82%%. The occupancy loss outweighed the stall reduction. Interesting: stall profile was excellent but couldn't compensate for 1/3 the warps.

optimization: BLOCK_K=16 + num_stages=4 for deeper software pipelining
hypothesis: Halve BLOCK_K to enable 4-stage pipelining at same SMEM budget, better hiding load latency
notes: 1.6%% speedup (0.1613->0.1587ms). Long Scoreboard -26%%, Short Scoreboard -18%%, SMEM reduced 32KB->24KB. Deeper pipelining better overlapped loads with compute. Barrier stall +51%% from 64 vs 32 iterations partially offset gains.

optimization: Fuse d dimension into program body, grid (H,N,d_k)->(H,N)
hypothesis: Fuse d dimension: grid from (H,N,d_k) to (H,N), each program computes full BLOCK_D output vector
notes: 36x speedup. Memory SOL 78.55->90.67%. V loads grew from scalar to vector but K/Q redundancy eliminated. WarpExecEff still 32% with BLOCK_D=64.

optimization: Query-side tiling with BLOCK_I=64, tl.dot for QK^T and PV
hypothesis: Add query-side tiling (BLOCK_I=64), each program processes 64 queries, reuses K/V loads 64x, uses tl.dot
notes: 13.6x over v1, 490x over v0. Tensor Core 44.57% (first use). Registers/Thread=168 (high). SMEM=80KB. Memory SOL still 78.7%.

hypothesis: Set num_stages=3 to hide global memory load latency behind computation
notes: No measurable effect. All metrics unchanged. Online softmax sequential dependency prevents effective pipelining of iterations. Confirms anti-pattern: num_stages>=3 not always better.

hypothesis: Shared memory tiling with tile-size=16 to reduce global memory latency
notes: 1.34x speedup. Global Load Efficiency 56→100%, L1 Bank Conflicts 32.8M→4.43M. New bottleneck: Barrier stall 5.96 from __syncthreads().

hypothesis: Fuse 2 K-tile loads per barrier cycle to reduce __syncthreads() overhead
notes: 1.6% improvement. Long Scoreboard dropped 5.46→3.31 (39%), but Barrier stall unchanged 5.96→6.30.

hypothesis: Fuse 4 K-tile loads per barrier cycle to further reduce __syncthreads() overhead
notes: 1.0% improvement — diminishing returns. Long Scoreboard dropped further 3.31→1.98. Barrier stall decreased slightly 6.30→5.76. Not Selected increased 3.96→4.55.

hypothesis: Increase K-tile size to 64 to naturally halve barrier calls
notes: 5.3% regression (0.6842→0.7200ms). Barrier stall jumped 5.76→8.51. Longer inner K loop (64 vs 16 iterations) increased barrier wait time. Branch targets 3x higher (557K→1.61M).

hypothesis: Thread coarsening — each thread computes 2 output elements to improve compute-to-barrier ratio and FMA utilization
notes: 1.31x speedup vs best prior (v3: 0.6842→0.5232ms). FFMA throughput jumped 862→1175/cycle (36% more). Each thread does 2x FMAs, better ILP. Global Load Efficiency 100→67% (non-coalesced B loads) but compute gain dominates. Overall 1.80x from v0 baseline.
